hooks.prompt: Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a ENGINEER (writing Svelte components, building features, fixing bugs). If you are NOT in a engineer role (e.g. you are an grader, tester, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this code quality review only applies to engineer sessions. If you ARE the engineer, proceed: Review this Svelte/TypeScript code change for domain-specific issues. File: $ARGUMENTS. Check for: 1) Legacy Svelte 4 patterns (writable/readable stores, $: reactive declarations, on:event instead of onevent) — these MUST use Svelte 5 runes ($state, $derived, $effect, $props, onclick). 2) Missing TypeScript strict compliance (any types, missing return types on exported functions). 3) Accessibility violations (missing aria attributes on interactive elements, click handlers without keyboard equivalents). 4) Performance concerns (unnecessary $effect when $derived would work, missing lazy loading for heavy components). Respond {"ok": true} or {"ok": false, "reason": "specific violation with line reference and fix suggestion"}.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if this session involved writing or editing Svelte/TypeScript source code as an engineering task (implementing features, fixing bugs, refactoring). If NO source code was written or edited in this session (e.g. this was a grading, testing, or debugging session), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this hook only applies to engineering sessions. If source code WAS written, check: 1) Were all requested features/fixes implemented? 2) Are there TODO comments or placeholder implementations left behind? 3) Were TypeScript types properly defined (no 'any' types)? 4) Were accessibility attributes added to interactive elements? 5) Was performance considered (lazy loading, code splitting for new routes)? 6) Are there any console.log statements that should be removed? Respond {"ok": true} if work appears complete, or {"ok": false, "reason": "specific incomplete items"}.
